question: What are the identifiable, documented patterns that make text read as AI-generated (especially Claude, but also GPT/Gemini family output), how can each be detected in a given passage, and what is the right fix for each — so they can be organised into scout lanes for an automated de-AI editing pass?

initial_facets.question: Lexical tells: which words/phrases are empirically overused in LLM output (excess vocabulary studies, e.g. Kobak et al., Liang et al.), and how do these lists drift by model and generation?

Syntactic and structural tells: rule of three, negative parallelism, em-dash overuse, colon reveals, low burstiness, signposting, summary closers, bolded-label bullets, heading overuse, excess formatting; how is each detected?
Rhetorical and tonal tells: sycophancy, hedging/false balance, inflated significance, vague attributions, promotional tone, empty conclusions, moralizing/disclaimers, enthusiasm, chatbot closers.
Content-level tells: generic over specific, missing concrete detail, hallucinated-sounding specifics, symmetric coverage, lack of stance, restating the question.
Model-specific signatures: what distinguishes Claude vs GPT vs Gemini prose (stylometry/attribution research, practitioner observations) and how tells shifted across 2024-2026 model generations.
Vendor style-steering guidance (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google docs on formatting, filler, verbosity) and existing humanizer/de-slop tools and prompts, including their known failure modes.
False positives and keep list: legitimate human/genre patterns that look AI-ish, and documented AI-detector biases (non-native writers, formulaic genres).
Fix guidance: what a good rewrite does for each pattern and what over-correction looks like (mechanical em-dash stripping, fake typos, synonym swapping).
Detection method reliability: how well do human readers, lexical lists, and automated detectors identify AI text, and what does that imply for a per-passage scout?

facets.question: Lexical tells: which words/phrases are empirically overused in LLM output (excess vocabulary studies, e.g. Kobak et al., Liang et al.), and how do these lists drift by model and generation?
facets.gap_note: Strong empirical lists (Kobak, Liang, Juzek&Ward, Geng&Trotta, Antislop, SpeechMap/ScriptGrain). Counterevidence: fixed lists near-random as detectors (Schmalz&Tack), drift, human adoption of delve.

facets.question: Syntactic and structural tells: rule of three, negative parallelism, em-dash overuse, colon reveals, low burstiness, signposting, summary closers, bolded-label bullets, heading overuse, excess formatting; how is each detected?
facets.gap_note: Wikipedia, humanizer, Reinhart (participial clauses/nominalizations), Graphite, Freeburg em-dash rates. Counterevidence: em-dash human rates vary widely; tech-doc genre conventions.

facets.question: Rhetorical and tonal tells: sycophancy, hedging/false balance, inflated significance, vague attributions, promotional tone, empty conclusions, moralizing/disclaimers, enthusiasm, chatbot closers.
facets.gap_note: Vendor docs, Model Spec, constitution, Sharma sycophancy, Wikipedia. Counterevidence: Zhou et al. LMs under-hedge on QA; warmth is a recommended voice.

facets.question: Content-level tells: generic over specific, missing concrete detail, hallucinated-sounding specifics, symmetric coverage, lack of stance, restating the question.
facets.gap_note: LAMP, slop taxonomy, Art or Artifice, homogenization. Counterevidence: creative-writing corpora may not transfer; fine-tuned AI preferred by experts.

facets.question: Model-specific signatures: what distinguishes Claude vs GPT vs Gemini prose (stylometry/attribution research, practitioner observations) and how tells shifted across 2024-2026 model generations.
facets.gap_note: Sun et al., Bitton, Reinhart, Graphite 2026, Signal Box, EQ-Bench, vendor docs. Gap: 2026 per-model evidence is mostly non-peer-reviewed industry research; Gemini tic list thin. Round 2: Economist Jul 2026 em-dash finding (via Daring Fireball/Fast Company) and Graphite Opus 5.5 update; Gemini evidence remains practitioner-only.

facets.question: Vendor style-steering guidance (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google docs on formatting, filler, verbosity) and existing humanizer/de-slop tools and prompts, including their known failure modes.
facets.gap_note: Anthropic/OpenAI/Google docs, de-slop skills, antislop, humanizer audits.

facets.question: False positives and keep list: legitimate human/genre patterns that look AI-ish, and documented AI-detector biases (non-native writers, formulaic genres).
facets.gap_note: Liang detector bias, Wikipedia ineffective indicators, Google style guide, Vinkers BMJ, Hyland. Counterevidence: vendor claims of low ESL FPR.

facets.question: Fix guidance: what a good rewrite does for each pattern and what over-correction looks like (mechanical em-dash stripping, fake typos, synonym swapping).
facets.gap_note: LAMP edit ops, humanizer rules, DAMAGE audit, vendor over-correction warnings.

facets.question: Detection method reliability: how well do human readers, lexical lists, and automated detectors identify AI text, and what does that imply for a per-passage scout?
facets.gap_note: Clark, Jakesch, Russell, OpenAI classifier withdrawal, Sadasivan, Krishna.

remaining_gaps: Gemini-specific prose tells rest on practitioner/vendor sources only (no peer-reviewed Gemini 2.5/3.x study found).
2026 per-model tell data for Claude Opus 5.x / GPT-6 / Gemini 3.x is from industry web research (Graphite, Signal Box, ScriptGrain, AI Writing Benchmark), not peer-reviewed.
The Economist July 2026 em-dash study, The Atlantic negative-parallelism piece and the Washington Post ChatGPT style analysis were paywalled; known via secondary quotes.
No peer-reviewed counts for signposting/throat-clearing phrases in nonfiction; underslop counts are a small self-published corpus.
Tells in non-English text not covered.
stop.basis: All active high-priority facets supported with direct evidence and counterevidence found after round 1; rounds 2, 3 and 5 added new sources (resetting the count); rounds 6 (vocabulary-probe) and 7 (disciplinary) were low-yield residual probes in distinct families targeting high-priority facets.
